'''Joshua O'Neal Jackson''' (born February 10, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for one season with the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] before declaring for the [[2017 NBA draft]].

==Early life==
Jackson was born in [[San Diego, California]]  while his mother, Apples Jones, was serving in the navy and lived there until he was eight months old when she moved them to Michigan to be closer to her family.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7142 |title=Josh Jackson Profile |website=University of Kansas Athletics Department |access-date=June 15, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Roberts |first=Ben |url=http://www.kentucky.com/2014/07/20/3344822/star-recruits-mom-says-hes-not.html |title=Star recruit's mom says he's not being recruited |newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=July 20, 2014 |accessdate=April 4, 2016}}</ref> He attended Consortium College Prep School in [[Detroit, Michigan]] his freshman and sophomore years, before moving to [[Napa, California]] to attend [[Justin-Siena High School]].

==High school career==
[[File:20160330 MCDAAG Josh Jackson and Jarrett Allen crash the offensive boards (1).jpg|thumb|left|Jackson crashing the offensive boards over Jarrett Allen in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald's All-American Game]]]]
As a freshman for the Consortium College Prep School, he averaged 17 [[Point (basketball)|points]], six [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], four [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] and four [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/-9035442000227782514/metro-detroit-boys-and-girls-basketball-freshman-of-the-year-josh-jackson-and-bailey-thomas-are-future-stars/ |title=Metro Detroit boys and girls basketball Freshman of the Year: Josh Jackson and Bailey Thomas are future stars - MLive.com |website=Highschoolsports.mlive.com |date= |accessdate=2016-04-06}}</ref> As a sophomore, he led the school to their first state title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/649699779975320672/josh-jackson-leads-detroit-consortium-basketball-to-first-class-c-title-breaks-silence-to-share-season-of-joy/ |title=Josh Jackson leads Detroit Consortium basketball to first Class C title, breaks silence to share season of joy - MLive.com |website=Highschoolsports.mlive.com |date= |accessdate=2016-04-06}}</ref> He averaged 28 points, 15 rebounds and six assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/2977845755363436201/josh-jackson-of-detroit-consortium-is-2014-mlive-detroit-player-of-the-year-for-boys-basketball/ |title=Josh Jackson of Detroit Consortium is 2014 MLive Detroit Player of the Year for boys basketball - MLive.com |website=Highschoolsports.mlive.com |date=2014-04-11 |accessdate=2016-04-06}}</ref>

Prior to his junior year, Jackson and his family moved to California to attend [[Justin-Siena High School]] in [[Napa, California]] and play for Prolific Prep.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/3889361316306006313/josh-jackson-announces-transfer-to-justin-siena-a-catholic-prep-school-in-california/ |title=Josh Jackson announces transfer to Justin-Siena, a Catholic prep school in California - MLive.com |website=Highschoolsports.mlive.com |date= |accessdate=2016-04-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.freep.com/article/20140726/HSS/307260040/Shawn-Windsor-Detroit-Prep-star-Josh-Jackson-is-chasing-his-dream-in-California |title=Detroit Free Press - Home |website=Archive.freep.com |date= |accessdate=2016-04-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Sernoffsky |first=Evan |url=http://www.sfgate.com/education/article/Basketball-star-headed-to-Napa-school-that-5658223.php |title=Basketball star headed to Napa school that doesn't yet exist |publisher=SFGate |date=2014-07-31 |accessdate=2016-04-06}}</ref> As a Junior, he averaged 31.2 [[points per game]] and 5.4 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]]. As a Senior, Jackson averaged 26.9 Points and 13.1 [[rebounds per game]]. Jackson played AAU basketball for 1Nation Elite, a program founded by his mother.<ref name=mother/> In March 2016, Jackson, played in the 2016 [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and joint led the scoring with 19 points, whilst also recording four rebounds and three assists. He was named Co-MVP alongside [[Frank Jackson (basketball)|Frank Jackson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/josh-jackson-does-some-of-everything-in-mcdonalds-all-american-game-win|title=Co-MVP Josh Jackson does some of everything in McDonald's All American Game win|website=USA Today High School Sports|language=en-US|access-date=2016-04-04}}</ref>

Jackson was a five-star recruit and is regarded as one of the top players in the 2016 class.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Josh-Jackson-140396 |title=Rivals |website=Sports.yahoo.com |date= |accessdate=2016-04-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/170377/josh-jackson |title=Josh Jackson - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN |website=Espn.go.com |date= |accessdate=2016-04-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/6594421n-josh-jackson |title=Josh Jackson, Prolific Prep SF - Scout |website=Scouthoops.scout.com |date= |accessdate=2016-04-06}}</ref>  He was ranked number one in the 2016 class by both [[Rivals.com]] and [[Scout.com]], while [[ESPN]] ranked him at number two behind only [[Harry Giles (basketball)|Harry Giles]].<ref name="JNewellKCStar04112016"/> [[247Sports.com]] ranked him both as the top rated player in the 2016 class along with giving him a 102 rating, the highest rating ever given to a recruit by the website.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://247sports.com/Article/Why-Kansas-signee-Josh-Jackson-is-so-special-45034992|title=Why Kansas signee Josh Jackson is so special|last=Meyer|first=Jerry|date=April 27, 2016|website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]]|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=|access-date=June 13, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
On April 11, 2016, Jackson tweeted that he would be attending the [[University of Kansas]] in [[Lawrence, Kansas]] to play basketball, picking KU over Michigan State and Arizona.<ref name="JNewellKCStar04112016">{{cite news |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=April 11, 2016 |title=No. 1 recruit Josh Jackson commits to KU basketball |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article71267547.html |newspaper=[[The Kansas City Star|Kansas City Star]] |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=April 13, 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/j_josh11/status/719684761216638976|title=Next year I will be attending Kansas University  #RCJHpic.twitter.com/rmBiF85n4J|first=Josh|last=Jackson|date=11 April 2016|publisher=}}</ref> During his only season at Kansas, Jackson showcased his all-around play between scoring, rebounding, play-making, and defending. Although he started as a power forward for the Jayhawks, not Jackson's normal positions of both small forward or shooting guard, he still recorded 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.7 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game with the team in his freshman season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kansas-freshman-josh-jackson-is-finally-off-to-the-nba-draft-and-could-be-no-1-pick/|title=Kansas freshman Josh Jackson is finally off to the NBA Draft and could be No. 1 pick|last=Norlander|first=Matt|date=April 17, 2017|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=June 14, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}}</ref> As a result of his efforts, he was named as an All-Big 12 First Team member, the Big 12 Freshman of the Year, was named as a second-team All-American according to Sporting News, and was also considered a third-team All-American according to the Associated Press and National Association of Basketball Coaches. On April 17, 2017, Jackson officially declared for the [[2017 NBA Draft]] and hired former [[Chicago Bulls]] point guard [[B. J. Armstrong]] as his agent, officially forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bleacherreport.com/articles/2697548-josh-jackson-declares-for-2017-nba-draft-signs-with-an-agent|title=Josh Jackson Declares for 2017 NBA Draft, Signs with an Agent|first=Mike |last=Chiari|publisher=}}</ref>

==Off the court==
===Personal life===
Jackson was raised by his mother Apple Jones and his stepfather Clarence Jones, who died in 2014 while Jackson was playing in a tournament in Las Vegas.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://thelab.bleacherreport.com/the-gamer/ |title=The Gamer |last=Couch |first=Greg |date=November 6, 2016 |work=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=June 15, 2017}}</ref>
Jackson's mother was a standout basketball player at the [[UTEP Miners women's basketball|University of Texas at El Paso]], transferring there after two years at [[Allen Community College]], but was only able to play for one season after being ruled academically ineligible for her senior year leading to her to leave UTEP and join the navy as a parachute rigger.<ref name="mother">{{Cite news |url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article47741045.html |title=Mother of nation’s No. 1 basketball prospect wants to change the way of high-level recruiting |last=Roberts |first=Ben |date=December 3, 2015 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |access-date=June 15, 2017}}</ref> Following Jackson's birth, Jones was invited to participate in the [[Washington Mystics]] training camp but eventually decided against participating, instead choosing to raise Jackson in Michigan.<ref name=mother/>

Jackson has cited chess and saxophone as his off the court passions, having started the chess club at Justin-Siena High School and having played the saxophone since he was in the seventh grade.<ref name="undefeated">{{Cite news |url=http://theundefeated.com/features/hes-got-a-game-to-match-his-mouth/ |title=He's Got A Game To Match His Mouth |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |date=June 28, 2016 |work=[[The Undefeated]] |access-date=June 15, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/josh-jackson-mcdonalds-all-american-michigan-state-josh-jackson-kansas-arizona-mcdaag |title=McDonald's All American Josh Jackson is two 'completely' different people on and off the court |last=Jordan |first=Jason |date=March 30, 2016 |work=[[USA Today|USA Today High School Sports]] |access-date=June 15, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article108556737.html |title=KU hoops notes: Freshman Josh Jackson proficient at saxophone as well as basketball |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=October 15, 2016 |work=[[Kansas City Star]] |access-date=June 15, 2017}}</ref>

===Vandalism case===
On February 2, 2017 it was reported by the [[Kansas City Star]] that Jackson and Kansas teammate LaGerald Vick were persons of interest in a vandalism case that had occurred the previous December outside a bar in [[Lawrence, Kansas|Lawrence]].
<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article130423344.html |title=KU players Josh Jackson, Lagerald Vick are persons of interest in vandalism investigation |last=Bauer |first=Laura |date=February 2, 2017 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2017 |last2=Williams |first2=Mará Rose}}</ref> It was alleged that Jackson and Vick had damaged the car of McKenzie Calvert, a KU women's basketball player and Vick's ex-girlfriend.<ref name="ap">{{Cite news |url=https://apnews.com/6b919e2c4c004a8c833b50a6376e5cf5/affidavit-josh-jackson-threatened-beat-womens-player |title=Affidavit: Josh Jackson threatened to 'beat' woman |last=Voigt |first=Kurt |date=March 17, 2017 |work=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=June 12, 2017}}</ref> She told police that during the incident outside the bar, Jackson yelled "for her to get out of the car and that he would beat her ass” prior to damaging her car.<ref name=ap/> Following the investigation by police, Jackson was charged with one count of misdemeanor criminal damage to property and was scheduled to be arraigned on April 12.<ref name="arraigned">{{Cite news |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article134735694.html |title=KU basketball star Josh Jackson won’t miss games after misdemeanor property damage charge |last=Bauer |first=Laura |date=February 24, 2017 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2017 |last2=Williams |first2=Mará Rose}}</ref> Following the announcement of the charges, Jackson released a statement apologizing for his role in the incident and offered to pay for damages.<ref name=arraigned/> Following Jackson's charges, KU basketball coach [[Bill Self]] stated that Jackson had been disciplined internally by the administration but would not be suspended for any games due to his actions in the incident.<ref name=arraigned/>

After pleading not guilty to the vandalism charges, Jackson filed for a diversion agreement in Douglas County Court which would last 12 months.
<ref name="diversion">{{Cite news |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article152020052.html |title=Former KU player Josh Jackson must apologize, attend anger management as part of diversion agreement |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=May 22, 2017 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2017}}</ref> As a part of the agreement Jackson agreed to complete an anger management course, complete community service, abstain from alcohol and drug use during the diversion period, obtain substance abuse evaluation and write a letter of apology to the victims.<ref name=diversion/> He also agreed to pay $250 in restitution, $158 to the court, and $150 for the cost of diversion.<ref name=diversion/> Although Jackson originally plead guilty, as a part of the diversion agreement he signed a stipulation of facts matching witness accounts of his actions during the incident.<ref name=diversion/> Following the successful completion of the diversion program, Jackson's case would be dismissed by the Douglas County Court.<ref name=diversion/> When asked about his progress during an interview on June 13, Jackson told reporters that he was nearly finished with the anger management course and that he had learned from his mistake.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article156265314.html|title=Josh Jackson says he’s ‘learned from the mistake’ with help from anger management class|last=Newell|first=Jesse|date=June 14, 2017|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|access-date=June 15, 2017|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lakersnation.com/lakers-workout-kansas-josh-jackson-video-interview/2017/06/13/|title=Josh Jackson’s Interview With The L.A. Media After His Workout (Video & Transcript)|last=Winters|first=Serena|date=June 13, 2017|website=Lakers Nation|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=|access-date=June 15, 2017|quote=There is truth to that. I have been taking an anger management course, I’m just about wrapping it up right now. It’s just something that I had to do, and I learned from the mistake that I made and I’m making it through it.}}</ref>
